library_preparation_preflight.summary: spring-boot-webmvc-test only pulls in spring-boot-test-autoconfigure and spring-boot-webmvc. @WebMvcTest, MockMvc and a servlet container need spring-test and the servlet API, and neither comes in transitively.

deterministic_setup.reason: MockMvc, MockMvcBuilders and the SpringExtension/TestContext framework that @WebMvcTest and its customizers rely on. Not a transitive dependency of spring-boot-webmvc-test. 7.0.9 is the Spring Framework version managed by Boot 4.1.1.
spring-boot-servlet and spring-webmvc do not bring the servlet API on the classpath. DispatcherServlet and MockHttpServletRequest need it. 6.1.0 is the version managed by Boot 4.1.1.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Use the existing scaffold conventions from sibling spring-boot-* test projects: testedLibraryVersion, assertj, and a conditional agent with a user-code-filter.json for org.springframework.boot packages. Prefer a programmatic setup that avoids needing a full Spring Boot application. Use AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext or AnnotationConfigServletWebApplicationContext with a small @Controller, and exercise WebMvcTypeExcludeFilter, WebMvcTestContextBootstrapper, MockMvcAutoConfiguration, MockMvcBuilderCustomizer and the SpringBootMockMvcBuilderCustomizer classes. If a @WebMvcTest or @SpringBootTest slice is attempted, a @SpringBootConfiguration class and the JUnit Platform and SpringExtension wiring are needed. A Jackson 3 JSON converter is only available if tools.jackson is on the classpath. spring-boot-http-converter is a runtime dependency, so no extra JSON dependency should be required unless the tests assert on JSON bodies. No Docker image or environment/system property is needed.
risks: Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) and Jackson 2 converter detection is classpath-dependent. Adding extra JSON libraries can change which metadata is exercised.
The full @WebMvcTest context bootstrap is reflection-heavy. If it fails under native-image, fall back to a manually assembled MockMvc setup.
The jakarta.servlet-api version may conflict if a tomcat-embed dependency is added later. Keep only one servlet API provider.
